forces.title: Weak European construction sector growth
forces.description: Europe's construction volumes are expected to grow by a marginal 0.5% in 2026, following declines in 2024. This subdued growth, influenced by higher financing costs and geopolitical risks, will cap momentum for demand in electrical components, cables, and parts used in building projects.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Robust infrastructure investment supporting demand
forces.description: Infrastructure investment across Europe, bolstered by EU funds and targeted spending on energy and digital networks, is providing a positive offset to the weak building sector. This continued investment fuels demand for electrical components, cables, and distribution transformers essential for upgrading and expanding critical infrastructure.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Increasing input costs and pricing pressure
forces.description: Higher energy prices are gradually pushing up production costs for energy-intensive materials in the construction sector. Simultaneously, contractors and producers of electrical components are finding it increasingly difficult to pass these higher input costs through the value chain, as end-customers (governments, businesses, homebuyers) already face elevated interest rates.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Supply chain disruptions from low water levels
forces.description: Low water levels in inland waterways are causing delays and increased transport costs for raw materials crucial to building materials production. This is leading to production constraints and material shortages for 8% of EU construction companies, which can impact the timely supply and cost of electrical components, cables, and parts in the construction supply chain.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Stalled residential construction growth due to macro factors
forces.description: Residential construction growth in the EU is stalling as building permit issuance has stabilised. Higher interest rates make new homes less affordable, geopolitical uncertainty reduces buyer confidence, and increased energy prices raise material costs. This slowdown directly impacts demand for electrical components, wiring devices, and lighting used in new residential builds.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Grid capacity constraints delaying Dutch construction
forces.description: In the Netherlands, limited grid capacity is actively delaying new electrical connections and construction projects. This, alongside nitrogen restrictions, creates significant setbacks for building developments, directly hindering the deployment of electrical components, cables, and parts within the region's construction sector.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Continued growth in EU energy infrastructure projects
forces.description: The EU energy construction sector has been consistently growing since 2022, driven by crucial investments in renewable energy and the expansion of electricity grids. This sustained focus on upgrading power infrastructure to support the energy transition and rising electricity demand provides a strong tailwind for electrical components, cables, and distribution transformers.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Significant investment in railway construction across EU
forces.description: Railway construction is experiencing strong growth across the EU, fueled by network renewals and major cross-border projects such as Rail Baltica and the Lyon-Turin rail link, as well as high-speed rail investments in Spain, Portugal, and Italy. This expansion of rail capacity will generate demand for associated electrical components, cables, and power distribution systems.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Growing demand for energy-efficient homes
forces.description: Higher energy prices are increasing the value premium for energy-efficient homes in Belgium, reinforcing a trend seen since the 2022 energy crisis. This encourages investments in insulation, high-performance glazing, and efficient heating systems, presenting a tailwind for electrical components, wiring devices, and potentially efficient motors or LED lighting in new and renovated energy-efficient buildings.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Belgian housing market cooling amid high interest rates
forces.description: The Belgian housing market, despite recent resilience, is expected to gradually cool, with nominal median house prices projected to increase by a modest 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027. Weaker mortgage lending and persistently high interest rates are dampening demand, creating a headwind for electrical components and related products in residential construction.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Energy transition investments driving freight demand
forces.description: Investments related to the energy transition and AI infrastructure in the Netherlands are generating additional freight demand. This broader economic activity and focus on new energy systems can indirectly support demand for electrical components, cables, and parts as industrial and commercial clients upgrade or expand operations.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Rising fuel and labor costs for logistics
forces.description: Road transport companies in the Netherlands face surging diesel prices (up 30% from 2025 due to the Iran war) and increasing labor costs (4% rise in driver wages). While fuel surcharges are typically passed on, the rapid increase creates temporary lags affecting profitability, potentially leading to higher logistics costs for electrical component manufacturers and distributors.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: New truck charge increasing logistics costs in Netherlands
forces.description: The introduction of a new truck charge in the Netherlands is prompting discussions with customers about reducing kilometres and improving efficiency in supply chains. While freight rates are rising to offset these costs, the full incorporation of the truck charging scheme in pricing structures in H2 2026 will test profitability, potentially increasing logistics expenses for electrical component manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Dutch road transport gains momentum despite truck charge

forces.title: Persistent global supply chain volatility
forces.description: Global supply chains are continuously impacted by geopolitical tensions, protectionism, and extreme weather, leading to operational challenges. While this creates opportunities for logistics providers, the resulting cost inflation from factors like fuel prices, wages, and interest rates, coupled with the difficulty of consistently passing costs to customers, presents a pervasive headwind for the manufacturing and distribution of electrical components.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Accelerating electrification in transport sector
forces.description: The transport sector is witnessing increasing electrification, supported by rapid growth in electric truck usage and new truck charging schemes, which are accelerating greenhouse gas emission reductions. This structural shift drives demand for various electrical components, cables, and charging infrastructure parts, providing a long-term tailwind for IN030203 manufacturers.
forces.source_title: Dutch transport and logistics proves resilient amid rising costs, global…

forces.title: Data center expansion drives power infrastructure demand
forces.description: Unprecedented capital expenditures by hyperscalers on AI infrastructure, primarily data centers, are fueling a surge in demand for power. This necessitates significant investments in supporting electrical infrastructure, including distribution transformers and associated cabling, to deliver the required energy, creating a substantial tailwind for manufacturers in IN030203.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Structural rise in global electricity demand
forces.description: Global electricity demand is projected to increase by approximately 3.1% annually, reaching 38,000 TWh by 2035, driven by industrial electrification and data center expansion. This structural shift underpins the 'transformer supercycle', necessitating a massive expansion of grid infrastructure and, consequently, a significant increase in demand for distribution transformers and related electrical components.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Growing global supply backlog for transformers
forces.description: The global transformer market is experiencing a severe supply-demand imbalance, resulting in a backlog exceeding 1,000 GVA by 2024 and projected to reach 1,690 GVA by 2030. This constrained supply environment, alongside robust demand from grid investment and electrification, translates to sustained high prices and extended lead times, creating a significant tailwind for manufacturers of distribution transformers within IN030203.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Energy constraints hinder European data center expansion
forces.description: The energy-intensive nature of AI data centers presents a significant challenge to their build-out. Europe specifically may lag other regions in overcoming current power constraints, including cost-related issues. This potential limitation on data center expansion in Europe could consequently dampen demand for the distribution transformers, cables, and other electrical components needed for these facilities.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Electrification of road transport drives demand for components
forces.description: The battery-electric vehicle (BEV) fleet is expanding at over 20% annually, driven by tightening emissions regulations and falling battery costs. This rapid electrification of road transport directly increases demand for various electrical components, power cables, and charging infrastructure, providing a significant and structural tailwind for the IN030203 sector in Europe.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Growing power demand from buildings and industry electrification
forces.description: Decarbonization efforts are accelerating the adoption of electric technologies like heat pumps in buildings and across various industries, contributing to overall rising electricity demand. This trend directly drives the need for upgraded and new electrical components, wiring devices, and distribution infrastructure within commercial and industrial settings, providing a consistent tailwind for the IN030203 sector.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Increased transformer demand from renewables deployment
forces.description: The rising share of renewables (to ~70% by 2035) significantly increases demand for transformers due to several factors: generation moving away from load centers, lower utilization rates requiring more installed capacity, and dispersed generation multiplying grid connection points. This necessitates numerous additional low- and medium-voltage transformers, creating a substantial tailwind for IN030203.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Surge in energy storage capacity driving transformer needs
forces.description: Energy storage capacity is projected to reach approximately 2,300 GW by 2035, growing at about 18% annually. Each increment of this expansion requires additional transformers capable of handling bidirectional power flows. This rapid growth in storage solutions presents a significant and direct tailwind for manufacturers of appropriate distribution transformers within the IN030203 sector.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Replacement cycle for aging grid infrastructure
forces.description: Much of Europe's and North America's grid infrastructure has exceeded its 25- to 40-year design life, with replacement accounting for over 30% of transformer demand. As failure rates climb after 30 years, this necessitates a continuous replacement cycle, often with larger units, providing a foundational and ongoing structural tailwind for distribution transformers and associated electrical components.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Strong growth projected for small/medium and distribution transformers
forces.description: The global transformer market is projected to reach 5,600 GVA by 2035, with small and medium power transformers expected to be the fastest-growing category at a CAGR of approximately 4%. Distribution transformers are also forecasted for solid growth at 3%. This targeted growth indicates sustained demand and opportunity for manufacturers within the IN030203 sector.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Production capacity constraints for transformers
forces.description: The transformer manufacturing base, fragmented globally, struggles to quickly scale up production. Building new plants is capital-intensive and slow, requiring specialized labor and facing long qualification cycles. Additionally, key inputs like grain-oriented electrical steel are in tight supply, collectively limiting new capacity and exacerbating the supply deficit, which benefits existing manufacturers in IN030203 through sustained high prices.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: European and North American transformer supply deficit
forces.description: In Europe and North America, domestic power transformer demand (914 GVA) significantly exceeded supply (566 GVA) by 38% in 2025, a gap expected to persist through 2030. Despite announced capacity additions, the annual supply shortfall will remain around 312 GVA, ensuring continued scarcity and favorable pricing conditions for manufacturers of distribution transformers within IN030203.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Limited impact of imports on European transformer deficit
forces.description: Europe and North America are increasing foreign sourcing of transformers, with net imports projected to double to 258 GVA by 2030. However, the impact is fundamentally limited by export countries' domestic demand, trade tariffs, localization requirements, and severe logistical constraints. This means the substantial supply deficit for transformers, including distribution types, will persist, sustaining favorable conditions for European IN030203 manufacturers.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Soaring transformer prices and extended lead times
forces.description: Transformer lead times have surged from about one year to up to five years, while market prices have increased by over 50% since 2021, reaching up to €8 per kVA. This dramatic shift of market power from buyers to suppliers, driven by persistent supply constraints, ensures continuously elevated pricing and lead times, creating a strong and sustained tailwind for manufacturers of distribution transformers in IN030203.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: High entry barriers protect incumbent transformer manufacturers
forces.description: The transformer industry is characterized by significant entry barriers, including multiyear capacity ramp-ups, a scarcity of skilled labor, lengthy product qualification periods, and increasing localization trends. These factors effectively protect incumbent manufacturers of distribution transformers within IN030203, allowing them to benefit from sustained demand and constrained supply without immediate threat from new market entrants.
forces.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

forces.title: Data center build-out boosts Norwegian electrical component demand
forces.description: The ongoing data center build-out in Norway is significantly increasing demand for essential electrical components, including cables, transformers, and switchboards. This specialized demand is a primary driver boosting activity and growth prospects for domestically oriented manufacturers in the Electrical Components, Cables & Parts sector (IN030203), providing a strong local tailwind.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Low construction activity dampens Norwegian economic growth
forces.description: Low construction activity, characterized by few new residential and commercial projects, is dampening overall economic growth in Norway. Although some contacts believe residential construction has troughed, the delayed upturn creates a sustained headwind for manufacturers of electrical components, cables, and parts whose demand is tied to building and development projects.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Wage growth impacting construction sector profitability
forces.description: Norwegian construction contacts report inability to significantly compensate for wage growth (estimated 4.5% in 2026, 4.0% in 2027) by raising prices. This squeeze on construction sector profitability, alongside fierce competition for contracts, creates a downstream headwind for suppliers like those in electrical components, cables, and parts, as buyers face budget constraints.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Automation investments in food and beverage industry
forces.description: Food and beverage producers are increasingly investing in automation, robotics, and integrated production methods to boost productivity, counteract labor shortages, and manage costs. This trend, involving the streamlining of operations and upskilling for automated environments, creates an upside driver for manufacturers of motors, VFDs, and other control components within the IN030203 sector, as industrial clients upgrade their facilities.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Modest recovery in Dutch housing construction
forces.description: Dutch housing construction is expected to stabilize in 2026 with 71,000 new-build homes, followed by slight growth to 74,000 in 2027, despite a 10-year high in permits. This modest recovery, hampered by project delays and slow translation of permits into starts, indicates a cautious positive outlook for electrical components and wiring devices in the residential sector in the Netherlands.
forces.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

forces.title: Slowdown in Dutch infrastructure sector growth
forces.description: The robust growth of the Dutch infrastructure sector, which saw 10.5% volume growth in 2025, is expected to slow significantly in 2026 and 2027. This deceleration is attributed to high construction costs, staff shortages, nitrogen restrictions, and limited government budgets prioritizing maintenance over new projects, creating a headwind for electrical components and cables supplied to this subsector.
forces.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

viewpoints.title: Transformer market in supercycle with demand outrunning supply
viewpoints.description: McKinsey identifies a 'transformer supercycle' where demand structurally outruns supply, driven by rising electricity demand, electrification, data center expansion, and the shift to renewables. This has led to a global supply backlog exceeding 1,000 GVA by 2024, projected to reach 1,690 GVA by 2030, fundamentally changing the market for all types of transformers, including distribution transformers, and creating strong market conditions for producers.
viewpoints.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

viewpoints.title: Strong growth expected for distribution and small/medium power transformers
viewpoints.description: McKinsey forecasts robust growth for distribution transformers (CAGR 3%) and particularly strong growth for small and medium power transformers (CAGR ~4% through 2035). This indicates a positive outlook for the IN030203 sector, which includes distribution transformers (<100 MVA), driven by overall market expansion, electrification trends, and the increasing demand for localized power management solutions.
viewpoints.source_title: The transformer supercycle: Why demand is outrunning supply

viewpoints.title: Norwegian manufacturers benefit from data center demand for electrical components
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network contacts report strong growth prospects for domestically oriented manufacturing in Norway, specifically for firms supplying cables, transformers, switchboards, and other energy supply equipment. This is directly driven by the ongoing data center build-out, indicating a positive outlook for the electrical components, cables & parts sector (IN030203) in the region.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Domestically-oriented manufacturing profitability boosted in Norway
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network contacts indicate that activity growth and higher prices are boosting profitability for domestically oriented manufacturing in Norway. This positive trend, which includes manufacturers of electrical components, cables, and parts (IN030203) catering to local demand (e.g., data center build-out), contrasts with the weak profitability seen in the construction sector and signals a favorable operating environment for these producers.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Dutch construction sector outlook remains fragile with limited growth
viewpoints.description: ING Research projects a fragile outlook for the Dutch construction sector, expecting zero growth in 2026 after contractions in Q1 and Q2, and only a modest 1% growth in 2027. This subdued performance, lagging the broader Dutch economy, suggests limited demand expansion for electrical components, cables, and parts directly tied to overall construction activity in the Netherlands.
viewpoints.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…
